commits.author: Hz_Zhang
commits.message:
Add blocking WAIT_PREFETCH_STATUS to avoid busy-polling the lookup wait (#3704)

* Add blocking WAIT_PREFETCH_STATUS to avoid busy-polling the lookup wait

The SGLang MP adapter's _wait_for_lookup busy-polled QUERY_PREFETCH_STATUS in
a 1ms sleep loop, adding repeated ZMQ requests and polling latency on the load
path -- noticeable when a lookup triggers movement from a slower storage layer
into L1 (per the TODO left in _wait_for_lookup).

Add a blocking WAIT_PREFETCH_STATUS request type. Its daemon handler blocks on
a PrefetchController completion condition variable until the prefetch result is
published (or a timeout), so the client issues a single request instead of
busy-polling. L1-only prefetches (prefetch_request_id == -1) return immediately.

Fixes #3694

Signed-off-by: Haozhe Zhang <zhang.hz6666@gmail.com>

* Register WAIT_PREFETCH_STATUS in the engine protocol definitions

The RequestType docstring requires every enum member to also have a protocol
definition (the validation system in protocols/__init__.py enforces a 1:1
match). The new WAIT_PREFETCH_STATUS member was missing one, so
initialize_protocols() would fail with an orphaned enum member. Add the
definition (payload: request_id str + timeout float, returns int | None) and
its REQUEST_NAMES entry, mirroring QUERY_PREFETCH_STATUS.

Signed-off-by: Haozhe Zhang <zhang.hz6666@gmail.com>

* test: cover the WAIT_PREFETCH_STATUS LookupModule handler path

Add targeted tests for wait_prefetch_status -> query_prefetch_status: count
computation + event emission + exactly-once job consumption on success, None +
job retention on timeout, and 0 for an unknown request_id. The storage manager is
mocked, so the request-handler/protocol path is exercised without a GPU or native
bitmap (the controller tests already cover the condition variable in isolation).

Signed-off-by: haozhe <haozhe@haozhes-MacBook-Pro.local>

* style: ruff-format the WAIT_PREFETCH_STATUS test

commits.author: Omer Rubinstein
commits.message:
feat(valkey): add per-key TTL + partial-chunk validation to Valkey glide connector (#3836)

* feat(valkey): reject partial/unfull chunks in Valkey glide connector

The Valkey GLIDE connector uses single-key, fixed-size storage with no
per-chunk metadata (same scheme as RESPConnector), so partial/unfull
chunks cannot be represented or verified on read. Validate this in
ValkeyConnectorAdapter by asserting save_chunk_meta and save_unfull_chunk
are both False, mirroring RESPConnectorAdapter.

Also coerce free-form extra_config booleans via _to_bool so a string
like "false" is parsed correctly (bool("false") is truthy); applied to
save_chunk_meta and the existing tls_enable read.

Additionally, harden _do_get_into so a short read is not silently
accepted: it previously returned True regardless of bytes read, leaving
stale tail bytes in the destination buffer and masking a size mismatch /
corruption. Warn and treat a size mismatch as a miss (return False) on
both the buffer-GET and legacy GET paths so the entry is recomputed.
Fixed-size KV chunks must round-trip exactly.

Tests cover the real _do_get_into buffer-GET return path directly, and
the in-memory mock now faithfully models the buffer-GET branch (returning
an int byte count) so get/batched_get are exercised on both GET paths.

Signed-off-by: Omer Rubinstein <omerrubi@amazon.com>

* feat(valkey): add optional per-key TTL to Valkey glide connector

Without a TTL, keys are persisted indefinitely, so a Valkey/Redis node
using a volatile-lru/volatile-lfu eviction policy never evicts the L2
KV cache keys and chokes once it reaches maxmemory. Add an opt-in,
configurable per-key TTL, gated behind a feature flag, so the eviction
policy can reclaim memory under pressure.

New extra_config keys:
- valkey_enable_ttl (bool, default false): feature flag.
- valkey_ttl_sec (int seconds, default 86400 when enabled but unset):
  per-key TTL; must be a positive integer.

_ThreadWorkerPool and ValkeyConnector accept ttl_seconds and, when set,
write keys with glide_sync.ExpirySet(SEC, ttl) (built lazily and cached;
the immutable ExpirySet is safe to share across worker threads). The
no-TTL path is unchanged. Adds docs and unit tests covering config
passthrough, defaulting, invalid-value rejection, and expiry application
on put.

Signed-off-by: Omer Rubinstein <omerrubi@amazon.com>

commits.author: nayeonikim
commits.message:
[Fix][RawBlock] Roll back put-task refs when dispatch scheduling fails (#3698)

batched_submit_put_task raises a ref on each pending object and reserves
its key in _put_tasks before handing the batch to the event loop. If
asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe fails (e.g. the loop is shutting down),
the raised refs and reserved keys for the unscheduled items leaked,
keeping the MemoryObj pinned and the key permanently blocked from future
puts. Wrap dispatch so the unscheduled items roll back their ref and
put-task entry; already-scheduled items still release theirs in the
coroutine's finally block.

commits.author: Tai An
commits.message:
fix(vllm/v1): no-op KV transfer when LMCache is in degraded mode (#3487)

* fix(vllm/v1): no-op KV transfer when LMCache is in degraded mode

When LMCache fails to initialize, the manager leaves `lmcache_engine` as
None and operates in degraded (recompute) mode. The worker-side
`start_load_kv`, `save_kv_layer`, and `wait_for_save` paths still
`assert self.lmcache_engine is not None`, which kills EngineCore on the
first request instead of honoring the documented recompute fallback.

Guard these entry points with an early return when the engine is None,
matching the existing degraded-mode handling in `_setup_metrics`. In
normal operation the engine is non-None so behavior is unchanged.

Signed-off-by: Tai An <antai12232931@outlook.com>

* fix(vllm/v1): guard scheduler-side hooks in degraded mode

Extend the degraded-mode handling to the four scheduler-side connector
hooks so a failed LMCache init no longer crashes EngineCore during
scheduling (per the matrix in vllm-project/vllm#44249):

- get_num_new_matched_tokens -> 0 (no external hit, recompute)
- update_state_after_alloc -> no-op
- build_connector_meta -> empty metadata
- request_finished -> (False, None)

Mirrors the existing worker-side guards; covers the "scheduler degraded
only" and "LMCache fully unavailable" rows that the worker-only guard
still let crash with EngineDeadError.

Signed-off-by: Tai An <antai12232931@outlook.com>

* fix(vllm/v1): don't short-circuit request_finished in degraded mode

The early return when lmcache_engine OR lookup_client is None dropped the
storage/lookup cancels that must still run when only one of the two is
missing. Remove it and rely on the per-branch fail-soft logic, which warns
and skips only the unavailable backend. Fixes the 4 regression tests in
tests/v1/test_v1_adapter_request_finished_scheduler_role.py (LMCache#3337).

commits.author: Boris Glimcher
commits.message:
feat: add concurrent batched_get_blocking to LocalDiskBackend (#3961)

LocalDiskBackend inherited the base class serial loop for
batched_get_blocking, calling get_blocking one key at a time.
This meant the hot read path (used by vLLM) got no I/O parallelism.

Override batched_get_blocking with a four-phase concurrent approach:
1. Batch metadata lookup under a single lock acquisition
2. Pre-allocate CPU staging buffers sequentially
3. Dispatch file reads to a ThreadPoolExecutor via map()
4. Update cache policy for successful loads

The GIL is released during readinto syscalls, so threads achieve
true I/O parallelism. The new _read_thread_pool is sized by the
existing disk_io_threads config (default 4), matching the GDS
backend pattern.

The read thread pool shutdown uses wait=True for consistent behavior
with LocalDiskWorker.close() and GdsBackend.close(), ensuring
in-flight reads complete gracefully before teardown.

commits.message:
feat: implement Cloud Bigtable L2 Adapter and Layer-Group Sharding optimizations (#3885)

* Implement Bigtable L2 Adapter and Layer-Group Sharding with Integration Fixes

This squashes the Bigtable storage backend connector and L2 daemon adapter implementation along with formatting and integration fixes.

Key Features & Optimizations:
- Integrated BigtableL2Adapter and BigtableL2KeyEncoder to support out-of-process remote L2 caching.
- Implemented Layer-Group Sharding inside the Bigtable connector to partition KV cache payloads along layer dimensions, bypassing Bigtable's single-cell limit.
- Added a thread-safe TTLCache wrapper inside lmcache/utils.py to shield Bigtable nodes from lookup spikes.
- Wrapped CPU-heavy payload sharding and reassembly inside loop.run_in_executor to prevent event loop blocking.
- Appended @lg{layer_group_size} configuration versioning to row keys to isolate sharding configurations.
- Bound CellsColumnLimitFilter(1) to all read queries to prevent database over-fetching.

Bug Fixes & Correctness:
- Aligned cell timestamps to millisecond granularity to prevent Bigtable emulator and server invalid timestamp errors.
- Resolved row key collisions in layerwise serving by suffixing @layer_{layer_id} in BigtableConnector and L2 adapter.
- Bypassed 200MB mutation size limits with concurrent split mutations and added 90MB single-shard safety warnings.
- Fixed V2 in-process memory exhaustion reference leak inside LMCacheEngine.retrieve by releasing reference counts for hits.
- Formatted all files with isort and ruff format to comply with Google Python style guide and pre-commit checks.

Signed-off-by: An Nguyen <annenguyen@google.com>

* fix(bigtable): L2 adapter correctness and performance fixes

- Offloaded memoryview-to-bytes conversion to executor thread pool.
- Fixed circuit breaker cache miss reset logic when no errors occur.
- Reconciled storage accounting (ghost bytes) on lookup and load cache misses.
- Rolled back lock refcounts on lookup cancellation or failure.
- Implemented size-based batch mutations chunking for unsharded bulk store.
- Added comprehensive unit tests for all correctness fixes.

commits.author: Omer Rubinstein
commits.message:
feat(valkey): Tag GLIDE connections as GlidePySync(lmcache:<ver>) (#4023)

* feat(valkey): Tag GLIDE connections as GlidePySync(lmcache:<ver>)

Attribute LMCache's valkey-glide connections in CLIENT INFO / CLIENT LIST
via GLIDE's client_info_tag option, producing GlidePySync(lmcache:<version>)
so LMCache usage is distinguishable without disturbing GLIDE's own library
identity or adoption metrics.

client_info_tag was added to the glide Python client in valkey-io/valkey-glide#6389
and ships in valkey-glide 2.5.0; it is not in any released wheel yet. Older
clients would raise TypeError on the unknown kwarg, so the connector applies
the tag only behind a feature-detection guard: it inspects the client config
constructor signature for a client_info_tag parameter and passes it through
in both the standalone and cluster branches of _ThreadWorkerPool._get_client
only when present. Behavior on current glide builds is unchanged.

The tag falls back to a bare "lmcache" if the resolved version string
contains whitespace (which GLIDE's config validation rejects).

Adds tests covering tag formatting, the whitespace fallback, signature-based
support detection, and that _get_client sets/omits the kwarg for supported
vs unsupported glide builds (standalone and cluster) using an injected fake
glide_sync module.

Signed-off-by: Omer Rubinstein <omerrubi@amazon.com>

* style(valkey): Fix isort import ordering in client_info_tag tests

isort (repo pre-commit hook, PyCQA/isort) orders the imported names
case-insensitively, placing _ThreadWorkerPool after the lowercase
helper functions. Reorder to satisfy the hook; local ruff check did not
flag it. No functional change.

Signed-off-by: Omer Rubinstein <omerrubi@amazon.com>

* test(valkey): Make client_info_tag test fake mypy-clean

CI mypy flagged the fake glide_sync helper: the config classes were
redefined under if/else (no-redef) and attributes were assigned onto a
types.ModuleType instance (attr-defined).

Rework the fake so it is statically clean:
- Define tagged vs untagged client/cluster config classes as distinct
  top-level classes (the differing constructor signatures are what the
  connector feature-detects) instead of redefining one name.
- Build the fake module as a types.SimpleNamespace rather than assigning
  attributes onto a ModuleType.
- Annotate the empty kwargs dict (var-annotated).

Verified locally: mypy, isort, ruff check/format all clean; 10 tests pass.

commits.author: weishu
commits.message:
[fix] Fix non-prefix  TP desync when a chunk's shard is missing on one TP rank (#4207)

fix(blend_v3): treat a single-rank CB retrieve miss as a whole-chunk gap

The SEGMENTED retained set in _poll_prefix_leg was computed by ORing the
per-rank shard bits ({ki // ws}), so a chunk whose shard failed to load on
one TP rank was still retained. That rank's retrieve then read a missing
object and desynced the TP engine. Retain a chunk only if EVERY rank's
shard loaded (AND), so a single-rank miss demotes the whole chunk to a
recompute gap uniformly across ranks.

Also stop echoing the client's own event handle on a failed retrieve
(self-importing it raises cudaErrorDeviceUninitialized on the client):
record and return a valid server event plus a False scatter-ran status.

* fix(mp): image-aware cache keys for multimodal requests

The MP connector fed raw token ids into lookup/store/retrieve key
derivation. vLLM emits identical placeholder token ids for every image,
so two requests with the same text but different images collided on the
same cache keys and could serve the wrong image's KV.

Capture mm hashes and placeholder positions in the request tracker,
materialize an mm-adjusted copy of the prompt token ids once (same
overwrite scheme the in-process adapter uses), and use it at every
key-derivation site so lookup, lock release, store, retrieve, and L0
telemetry stay consistent.

commits.author: Dongjoo Seo
commits.message:
[MP][DAX] coalesce DAX L2 load path : per-device batching, copies outside the adapter lock (#4010)

* dax: coalesce L2 load path — batch per device, copy outside the adapter lock, parallel sub-batches

_execute_load_task previously copied a request's chunks one at a time:
each chunk went through load_many_into() with a batch of one (paying the
full slot-reservation cycle per chunk), all copies ran sequentially on a
single load worker, and the adapter-global _device_lock was held across
the entire batch, serializing concurrent requests' loads against each
other.

This change:
- groups the batch's keys per device under _device_lock (dict lookups
  only), releasing the lock before any data movement — per-device cores
  already take their own reservation locks;
- issues real per-device batches to load_many_into(), amortizing the
  reservation cycle;
- splits groups into ~0.5 GiB sub-batches copied via an inline thread
  pool; ctypes.memmove releases the GIL, so the copies overlap.

A/B measured on CXL devdax (identical setup: one lane, 6 x 32 GiB
devices, 8 x 43k-char Qwen2.5-32B prompts, concurrency 4, reuse after L1
clear):
  reuse mean TTFT   5683 ms -> 3307 ms  (1.72x)
  reuse p99  TTFT   7116 ms -> 4727 ms  (1.51x)
  prefetch p50 (44 chunks, 2.75 GiB)  ~2040 -> ~1550 ms
  prefetch worst    2811 ms -> 1630 ms
  fill TTFT unchanged (load-path-only change)
The stock tail (2.7-2.8 s prefetches) is requests queueing behind the
adapter-global lock while another batch copies; removing that
serialization is the dominant win and grows with MP-server concurrency.
Raw medium bandwidth is 5.3 GB/s single-thread / 23 GB/s at 8 threads
(GIL-free memcpy); the remaining gap is dominated by per-request L1
staging-buffer allocation above this adapter, left as follow-up.

Co-authored-by: Dongjoo Seo <dongjoo.seo1@samsung.com>
Signed-off-by: DongDongJu <commisori28@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Dongjoo Seo <dongjoo.seo1@samsung.com>

* dax: address review — per-sub-batch error isolation, persistent copy pool, device_id keys

- _load_sub now catches per-sub-batch failures and returns per-key False
  flags, so one failing device/sub-batch no longer discards the results
  of sub-batches that loaded successfully.
- Replace the per-call inline ThreadPoolExecutor with a persistent
  self._copy_executor (created with the other executors, shut down after
  the load executor in close(), since load tasks fan out to it). Removes
  thread create/destroy from the TTFT-critical path and caps total copy
  parallelism across concurrent load tasks; falls back to inline copies
  if the pool is unavailable.
- Key device groups by entry.device_id instead of id(entry).

commits.author: Arijit Desai
commits.message:
fix(pd): fail fast when a prefill exceeds the receiver buffer capacity (#4210)

The receiver's reservation admission only succeeds when the buffer has
enough free chunks (`available >= total_chunks`), and `available` can
never exceed the buffer's total capacity. A request whose declared
`total_chunks` is larger than the whole buffer therefore can never be
admitted: it blocked for the full `pd_allocation_timeout_sec` and then
raised a misleading "over-subscribed" timeout, tearing down the transfer
mid-flight (clients saw ServerDisconnectedError / "Not enough data to
satisfy transfer length header").

Add an explicit fail-fast in `_async_allocate_and_put`, co-located with
the existing `total_chunks == 0` validation, that rejects such a request
immediately with an actionable error (needs N chunks, buffer holds M,
increase pd_buffer_size). Add a regression test asserting the request is
rejected well before the admission timeout could elapse and leaves no
reservation behind.

commits.author: Libin Tang
commits.message:
xpu: pin LMCache host buffer via sycl::malloc_host (#4129)

* xpu: pin LMCache host buffer via sycl::malloc_host

The local_cpu backend host buffer was never pinned on XPU: the pinned-alloc
path (lmc_ops.alloc_pinned_ptr) is CUDA-only (cudaHostAlloc) and is not
compiled into xpu_ops, so allocation silently fell back to pageable host
memory -> D2H KV store ran at ~1.5 GB/s.

Add a SYCL analog alloc_pinned_ptr/free_pinned_ptr (sycl::malloc_host on the
current XPU device context) bound under the same names as the CUDA ops, so
lmcache._get_backend() overrides them by name on XPU with no device-specific
branching in _allocate_cpu_memory/_free_cpu_memory. Restores true USM-pinned
host memory -> D2H store ~10-30 GB/s (~20x).

sycl::malloc_host is capped at the device max_mem_alloc_size (~30 GiB on B70
= 95% of one card's VRAM), so a large max_local_cpu_size can overflow it.
Add a device-agnostic pageable fallback (with a warning) so the engine
degrades gracefully instead of crashing; torch pin_memory=True is avoided
because torch XPU pinned buffers segfault on access above ~16 GiB. shm /
NUMA / hugepage allocations are excluded from the fallback since a plain
pageable buffer cannot preserve their semantics.

Split out of #4022 (pin-memory allocation only); the SGLang connector logic
changes in that PR are being tracked separately.

commits.author: Hz_Zhang
commits.message:
Add blocking WAIT_PREFETCH_STATUS to avoid busy-polling the lookup wait (#3704)

* Add blocking WAIT_PREFETCH_STATUS to avoid busy-polling the lookup wait

The SGLang MP adapter's _wait_for_lookup busy-polled QUERY_PREFETCH_STATUS in
a 1ms sleep loop, adding repeated ZMQ requests and polling latency on the load
path -- noticeable when a lookup triggers movement from a slower storage layer
into L1 (per the TODO left in _wait_for_lookup).

Add a blocking WAIT_PREFETCH_STATUS request type. Its daemon handler blocks on
a PrefetchController completion condition variable until the prefetch result is
published (or a timeout), so the client issues a single request instead of
busy-polling. L1-only prefetches (prefetch_request_id == -1) return immediately.

Fixes #3694

Signed-off-by: Haozhe Zhang <zhang.hz6666@gmail.com>

* Register WAIT_PREFETCH_STATUS in the engine protocol definitions

The RequestType docstring requires every enum member to also have a protocol
definition (the validation system in protocols/__init__.py enforces a 1:1
match). The new WAIT_PREFETCH_STATUS member was missing one, so
initialize_protocols() would fail with an orphaned enum member. Add the
definition (payload: request_id str + timeout float, returns int | None) and
its REQUEST_NAMES entry, mirroring QUERY_PREFETCH_STATUS.

Signed-off-by: Haozhe Zhang <zhang.hz6666@gmail.com>

* test: cover the WAIT_PREFETCH_STATUS LookupModule handler path

Add targeted tests for wait_prefetch_status -> query_prefetch_status: count

job retention on timeout, and 0 for an unknown request_id. The storage manager is
mocked, so the request-handler/protocol path is exercised without a GPU or native
bitmap (the controller tests already cover the condition variable in isolation).

commits.author: Omer Rubinstein
commits.message:
feat(valkey): add per-key TTL + partial-chunk validation to Valkey glide connector (#3836)

* feat(valkey): reject partial/unfull chunks in Valkey glide connector

The Valkey GLIDE connector uses single-key, fixed-size storage with no
per-chunk metadata (same scheme as RESPConnector), so partial/unfull
chunks cannot be represented or verified on read. Validate this in
ValkeyConnectorAdapter by asserting save_chunk_meta and save_unfull_chunk
are both False, mirroring RESPConnectorAdapter.

Also coerce free-form extra_config booleans via _to_bool so a string
like "false" is parsed correctly (bool("false") is truthy); applied to
save_chunk_meta and the existing tls_enable read.

Additionally, harden _do_get_into so a short read is not silently
accepted: it previously returned True regardless of bytes read, leaving
stale tail bytes in the destination buffer and masking a size mismatch /
corruption. Warn and treat a size mismatch as a miss (return False) on
both the buffer-GET and legacy GET paths so the entry is recomputed.
Fixed-size KV chunks must round-trip exactly.

Tests cover the real _do_get_into buffer-GET return path directly, and
the in-memory mock now faithfully models the buffer-GET branch (returning
an int byte count) so get/batched_get are exercised on both GET paths.

Signed-off-by: Omer Rubinstein <omerrubi@amazon.com>

* feat(valkey): add optional per-key TTL to Valkey glide connector

Without a TTL, keys are persisted indefinitely, so a Valkey/Redis node
using a volatile-lru/volatile-lfu eviction policy never evicts the L2
KV cache keys and chokes once it reaches maxmemory. Add an opt-in,
configurable per-key TTL, gated behind a feature flag, so the eviction
policy can reclaim memory under pressure.

New extra_config keys:
- valkey_enable_ttl (bool, default false): feature flag.
- valkey_ttl_sec (int seconds, default 86400 when enabled but unset):
  per-key TTL; must be a positive integer.

_ThreadWorkerPool and ValkeyConnector accept ttl_seconds and, when set,
write keys with glide_sync.ExpirySet(SEC, ttl) (built lazily and cached;
the immutable ExpirySet is safe to share across worker threads). The
no-TTL path is unchanged. Adds docs and unit tests covering config
passthrough, defaulting, invalid-value rejection, and expiry application
on put.

commits.author: nayeonikim
commits.message:
[Fix][RawBlock] Roll back put-task refs when dispatch scheduling fails (#3698)

batched_submit_put_task raises a ref on each pending object and reserves
its key in _put_tasks before handing the batch to the event loop. If
asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe fails (e.g. the loop is shutting down),
the raised refs and reserved keys for the unscheduled items leaked,
keeping the MemoryObj pinned and the key permanently blocked from future
puts. Wrap dispatch so the unscheduled items roll back their ref and
put-task entry; already-scheduled items still release theirs in the
coroutine's finally block.

commits.author: Dongjoo Seo
commits.message:
[MP][DAX] coalesce DAX L2 load path : per-device batching, copies outside the adapter lock (#4010)

* dax: coalesce L2 load path — batch per device, copy outside the adapter lock, parallel sub-batches

_execute_load_task previously copied a request's chunks one at a time:
each chunk went through load_many_into() with a batch of one (paying the
full slot-reservation cycle per chunk), all copies ran sequentially on a
single load worker, and the adapter-global _device_lock was held across
the entire batch, serializing concurrent requests' loads against each
other.

This change:
- groups the batch's keys per device under _device_lock (dict lookups
  only), releasing the lock before any data movement — per-device cores
  already take their own reservation locks;
- issues real per-device batches to load_many_into(), amortizing the
  reservation cycle;
- splits groups into ~0.5 GiB sub-batches copied via an inline thread
  pool; ctypes.memmove releases the GIL, so the copies overlap.

A/B measured on CXL devdax (identical setup: one lane, 6 x 32 GiB
devices, 8 x 43k-char Qwen2.5-32B prompts, concurrency 4, reuse after L1
clear):
  reuse mean TTFT   5683 ms -> 3307 ms  (1.72x)
  reuse p99  TTFT   7116 ms -> 4727 ms  (1.51x)
  prefetch p50 (44 chunks, 2.75 GiB)  ~2040 -> ~1550 ms
  prefetch worst    2811 ms -> 1630 ms
  fill TTFT unchanged (load-path-only change)
The stock tail (2.7-2.8 s prefetches) is requests queueing behind the
adapter-global lock while another batch copies; removing that
serialization is the dominant win and grows with MP-server concurrency.
Raw medium bandwidth is 5.3 GB/s single-thread / 23 GB/s at 8 threads
(GIL-free memcpy); the remaining gap is dominated by per-request L1
staging-buffer allocation above this adapter, left as follow-up.

Co-authored-by: Dongjoo Seo <dongjoo.seo1@samsung.com>
Signed-off-by: DongDongJu <commisori28@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Dongjoo Seo <dongjoo.seo1@samsung.com>

* dax: address review — per-sub-batch error isolation, persistent copy pool, device_id keys

- _load_sub now catches per-sub-batch failures and returns per-key False
  flags, so one failing device/sub-batch no longer discards the results
  of sub-batches that loaded successfully.
- Replace the per-call inline ThreadPoolExecutor with a persistent
  self._copy_executor (created with the other executors, shut down after
  the load executor in close(), since load tasks fan out to it). Removes
  thread create/destroy from the TTFT-critical path and caps total copy
  parallelism across concurrent load tasks; falls back to inline copies
  if the pool is unavailable.
- Key device groups by entry.device_id instead of id(entry).

fix(vllm/v1): no-op KV transfer when LMCache is in degraded mode (#3487)

* fix(vllm/v1): no-op KV transfer when LMCache is in degraded mode

When LMCache fails to initialize, the manager leaves `lmcache_engine` as
None and operates in degraded (recompute) mode. The worker-side
`start_load_kv`, `save_kv_layer`, and `wait_for_save` paths still
`assert self.lmcache_engine is not None`, which kills EngineCore on the
first request instead of honoring the documented recompute fallback.

Guard these entry points with an early return when the engine is None,
matching the existing degraded-mode handling in `_setup_metrics`. In
normal operation the engine is non-None so behavior is unchanged.

Signed-off-by: Tai An <antai12232931@outlook.com>

* fix(vllm/v1): guard scheduler-side hooks in degraded mode

Extend the degraded-mode handling to the four scheduler-side connector
hooks so a failed LMCache init no longer crashes EngineCore during
scheduling (per the matrix in vllm-project/vllm#44249):

- get_num_new_matched_tokens -> 0 (no external hit, recompute)
- update_state_after_alloc -> no-op
- build_connector_meta -> empty metadata

commits.message:
feat: add concurrent batched_get_blocking to LocalDiskBackend (#3961)

LocalDiskBackend inherited the base class serial loop for
batched_get_blocking, calling get_blocking one key at a time.
This meant the hot read path (used by vLLM) got no I/O parallelism.

Override batched_get_blocking with a four-phase concurrent approach:
1. Batch metadata lookup under a single lock acquisition
2. Pre-allocate CPU staging buffers sequentially
3. Dispatch file reads to a ThreadPoolExecutor via map()
4. Update cache policy for successful loads

The GIL is released during readinto syscalls, so threads achieve
true I/O parallelism. The new _read_thread_pool is sized by the
existing disk_io_threads config (default 4), matching the GDS
backend pattern.

The read thread pool shutdown uses wait=True for consistent behavior
with LocalDiskWorker.close() and GdsBackend.close(), ensuring
in-flight reads complete gracefully before teardown.

Attribute LMCache's valkey-glide connections in CLIENT INFO / CLIENT LIST
via GLIDE's client_info_tag option, producing GlidePySync(lmcache:<version>)
so LMCache usage is distinguishable without disturbing GLIDE's own library
identity or adoption metrics.

client_info_tag was added to the glide Python client in valkey-io/valkey-glide#6389
and ships in valkey-glide 2.5.0; it is not in any released wheel yet. Older
clients would raise TypeError on the unknown kwarg, so the connector applies
the tag only behind a feature-detection guard: it inspects the client config
constructor signature for a client_info_tag parameter and passes it through
in both the standalone and cluster branches of _ThreadWorkerPool._get_client
only when present. Behavior on current glide builds is unchanged.

The tag falls back to a bare "lmcache" if the resolved version string
contains whitespace (which GLIDE's config validation rejects).

Adds tests covering tag formatting, the whitespace fallback, signature-based
support detection, and that _get_client sets/omits the kwarg for supported
vs unsupported glide builds (standalone and cluster) using an injected fake
glide_sync module.

commits.author: Arijit Desai
commits.message:
fix(pd): fail fast when a prefill exceeds the receiver buffer capacity (#4210)

The receiver's reservation admission only succeeds when the buffer has
enough free chunks (`available >= total_chunks`), and `available` can
never exceed the buffer's total capacity. A request whose declared
`total_chunks` is larger than the whole buffer therefore can never be
admitted: it blocked for the full `pd_allocation_timeout_sec` and then
raised a misleading "over-subscribed" timeout, tearing down the transfer
mid-flight (clients saw ServerDisconnectedError / "Not enough data to
satisfy transfer length header").

Add an explicit fail-fast in `_async_allocate_and_put`, co-located with
the existing `total_chunks == 0` validation, that rejects such a request
immediately with an actionable error (needs N chunks, buffer holds M,
increase pd_buffer_size). Add a regression test asserting the request is
rejected well before the admission timeout could elapse and leaves no
reservation behind.

commits.author: Libin Tang
commits.message:
xpu: pin LMCache host buffer via sycl::malloc_host (#4129)

* xpu: pin LMCache host buffer via sycl::malloc_host

The local_cpu backend host buffer was never pinned on XPU: the pinned-alloc
path (lmc_ops.alloc_pinned_ptr) is CUDA-only (cudaHostAlloc) and is not
compiled into xpu_ops, so allocation silently fell back to pageable host
memory -> D2H KV store ran at ~1.5 GB/s.

Add a SYCL analog alloc_pinned_ptr/free_pinned_ptr (sycl::malloc_host on the
current XPU device context) bound under the same names as the CUDA ops, so
lmcache._get_backend() overrides them by name on XPU with no device-specific
branching in _allocate_cpu_memory/_free_cpu_memory. Restores true USM-pinned
host memory -> D2H store ~10-30 GB/s (~20x).

sycl::malloc_host is capped at the device max_mem_alloc_size (~30 GiB on B70
= 95% of one card's VRAM), so a large max_local_cpu_size can overflow it.
Add a device-agnostic pageable fallback (with a warning) so the engine
degrades gracefully instead of crashing; torch pin_memory=True is avoided
because torch XPU pinned buffers segfault on access above ~16 GiB. shm /
NUMA / hugepage allocations are excluded from the fallback since a plain
pageable buffer cannot preserve their semantics.

Split out of #4022 (pin-memory allocation only); the SGLang connector logic
changes in that PR are being tracked separately.

commits.message:
Add blocking WAIT_PREFETCH_STATUS to avoid busy-polling the lookup wait (#3704)

* Add blocking WAIT_PREFETCH_STATUS to avoid busy-polling the lookup wait

The SGLang MP adapter's _wait_for_lookup busy-polled QUERY_PREFETCH_STATUS in
a 1ms sleep loop, adding repeated ZMQ requests and polling latency on the load
path -- noticeable when a lookup triggers movement from a slower storage layer
into L1 (per the TODO left in _wait_for_lookup).

Add a blocking WAIT_PREFETCH_STATUS request type. Its daemon handler blocks on
a PrefetchController completion condition variable until the prefetch result is
published (or a timeout), so the client issues a single request instead of
busy-polling. L1-only prefetches (prefetch_request_id == -1) return immediately.

Fixes #3694

Signed-off-by: Haozhe Zhang <zhang.hz6666@gmail.com>

* Register WAIT_PREFETCH_STATUS in the engine protocol definitions

The RequestType docstring requires every enum member to also have a protocol
definition (the validation system in protocols/__init__.py enforces a 1:1
match). The new WAIT_PREFETCH_STATUS member was missing one, so
initialize_protocols() would fail with an orphaned enum member. Add the
definition (payload: request_id str + timeout float, returns int | None) and
its REQUEST_NAMES entry, mirroring QUERY_PREFETCH_STATUS.

Signed-off-by: Haozhe Zhang <zhang.hz6666@gmail.com>

* test: cover the WAIT_PREFETCH_STATUS LookupModule handler path

Add targeted tests for wait_prefetch_status -> query_prefetch_status: count
computation + event emission + exactly-once job consumption on success, None +
job retention on timeout, and 0 for an unknown request_id. The storage manager is
mocked, so the request-handler/protocol path is exercised without a GPU or native
bitmap (the controller tests already cover the condition variable in isolation).

commits.author: Omer Rubinstein
commits.message:
feat(valkey): add per-key TTL + partial-chunk validation to Valkey glide connector (#3836)

* feat(valkey): reject partial/unfull chunks in Valkey glide connector

The Valkey GLIDE connector uses single-key, fixed-size storage with no
per-chunk metadata (same scheme as RESPConnector), so partial/unfull
chunks cannot be represented or verified on read. Validate this in
ValkeyConnectorAdapter by asserting save_chunk_meta and save_unfull_chunk
are both False, mirroring RESPConnectorAdapter.

Also coerce free-form extra_config booleans via _to_bool so a string
like "false" is parsed correctly (bool("false") is truthy); applied to
save_chunk_meta and the existing tls_enable read.

Additionally, harden _do_get_into so a short read is not silently
accepted: it previously returned True regardless of bytes read, leaving
stale tail bytes in the destination buffer and masking a size mismatch /
corruption. Warn and treat a size mismatch as a miss (return False) on
both the buffer-GET and legacy GET paths so the entry is recomputed.
Fixed-size KV chunks must round-trip exactly.

Tests cover the real _do_get_into buffer-GET return path directly, and
the in-memory mock now faithfully models the buffer-GET branch (returning
an int byte count) so get/batched_get are exercised on both GET paths.

Signed-off-by: Omer Rubinstein <omerrubi@amazon.com>

* feat(valkey): add optional per-key TTL to Valkey glide connector

Without a TTL, keys are persisted indefinitely, so a Valkey/Redis node
using a volatile-lru/volatile-lfu eviction policy never evicts the L2
KV cache keys and chokes once it reaches maxmemory. Add an opt-in,
configurable per-key TTL, gated behind a feature flag, so the eviction
policy can reclaim memory under pressure.

New extra_config keys:
- valkey_enable_ttl (bool, default false): feature flag.
- valkey_ttl_sec (int seconds, default 86400 when enabled but unset):
  per-key TTL; must be a positive integer.

_ThreadWorkerPool and ValkeyConnector accept ttl_seconds and, when set,
write keys with glide_sync.ExpirySet(SEC, ttl) (built lazily and cached;
the immutable ExpirySet is safe to share across worker threads). The
no-TTL path is unchanged. Adds docs and unit tests covering config
passthrough, defaulting, invalid-value rejection, and expiry application
on put.

Signed-off-by: Omer Rubinstein <omerrubi@amazon.com>

commits.author: nayeonikim
commits.message:
[Fix][RawBlock] Roll back put-task refs when dispatch scheduling fails (#3698)

batched_submit_put_task raises a ref on each pending object and reserves
its key in _put_tasks before handing the batch to the event loop. If
asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe fails (e.g. the loop is shutting down),
the raised refs and reserved keys for the unscheduled items leaked,
keeping the MemoryObj pinned and the key permanently blocked from future
puts. Wrap dispatch so the unscheduled items roll back their ref and
put-task entry; already-scheduled items still release theirs in the
coroutine's finally block.

Signed-off-by: Nayeon Kim <nayeoni.kim@samsung.com>

[fix] Fix non-prefix  TP desync when a chunk's shard is missing on one TP rank (#4207)

fix(blend_v3): treat a single-rank CB retrieve miss as a whole-chunk gap

The SEGMENTED retained set in _poll_prefix_leg was computed by ORing the
per-rank shard bits ({ki // ws}), so a chunk whose shard failed to load on
one TP rank was still retained. That rank's retrieve then read a missing
object and desynced the TP engine. Retain a chunk only if EVERY rank's

recompute gap uniformly across ranks.

commits.author: Dongjoo Seo
commits.message:
[MP][DAX] coalesce DAX L2 load path : per-device batching, copies outside the adapter lock (#4010)

* dax: coalesce L2 load path — batch per device, copy outside the adapter lock, parallel sub-batches

_execute_load_task previously copied a request's chunks one at a time:
each chunk went through load_many_into() with a batch of one (paying the
full slot-reservation cycle per chunk), all copies ran sequentially on a
single load worker, and the adapter-global _device_lock was held across
the entire batch, serializing concurrent requests' loads against each
other.

This change:
- groups the batch's keys per device under _device_lock (dict lookups
  only), releasing the lock before any data movement — per-device cores
  already take their own reservation locks;
- issues real per-device batches to load_many_into(), amortizing the
  reservation cycle;
- splits groups into ~0.5 GiB sub-batches copied via an inline thread
  pool; ctypes.memmove releases the GIL, so the copies overlap.

A/B measured on CXL devdax (identical setup: one lane, 6 x 32 GiB
devices, 8 x 43k-char Qwen2.5-32B prompts, concurrency 4, reuse after L1
clear):
  reuse mean TTFT   5683 ms -> 3307 ms  (1.72x)
  reuse p99  TTFT   7116 ms -> 4727 ms  (1.51x)
  prefetch p50 (44 chunks, 2.75 GiB)  ~2040 -> ~1550 ms
  prefetch worst    2811 ms -> 1630 ms
  fill TTFT unchanged (load-path-only change)
The stock tail (2.7-2.8 s prefetches) is requests queueing behind the
adapter-global lock while another batch copies; removing that
serialization is the dominant win and grows with MP-server concurrency.
Raw medium bandwidth is 5.3 GB/s single-thread / 23 GB/s at 8 threads
(GIL-free memcpy); the remaining gap is dominated by per-request L1
staging-buffer allocation above this adapter, left as follow-up.

commits.message:
feat: add concurrent batched_get_blocking to LocalDiskBackend (#3961)

LocalDiskBackend inherited the base class serial loop for
batched_get_blocking, calling get_blocking one key at a time.
This meant the hot read path (used by vLLM) got no I/O parallelism.

Override batched_get_blocking with a four-phase concurrent approach:
1. Batch metadata lookup under a single lock acquisition
2. Pre-allocate CPU staging buffers sequentially
3. Dispatch file reads to a ThreadPoolExecutor via map()
4. Update cache policy for successful loads

The GIL is released during readinto syscalls, so threads achieve
true I/O parallelism. The new _read_thread_pool is sized by the
existing disk_io_threads config (default 4), matching the GDS
backend pattern.

The read thread pool shutdown uses wait=True for consistent behavior
with LocalDiskWorker.close() and GdsBackend.close(), ensuring
in-flight reads complete gracefully before teardown.

* Implement Bigtable L2 Adapter and Layer-Group Sharding with Integration Fixes

This squashes the Bigtable storage backend connector and L2 daemon adapter implementation along with formatting and integration fixes.

Key Features & Optimizations:
- Integrated BigtableL2Adapter and BigtableL2KeyEncoder to support out-of-process remote L2 caching.
- Implemented Layer-Group Sharding inside the Bigtable connector to partition KV cache payloads along layer dimensions, bypassing Bigtable's single-cell limit.
- Added a thread-safe TTLCache wrapper inside lmcache/utils.py to shield Bigtable nodes from lookup spikes.
- Wrapped CPU-heavy payload sharding and reassembly inside loop.run_in_executor to prevent event loop blocking.
- Appended @lg{layer_group_size} configuration versioning to row keys to isolate sharding configurations.
- Bound CellsColumnLimitFilter(1) to all read queries to prevent database over-fetching.

Bug Fixes & Correctness:
- Aligned cell timestamps to millisecond granularity to prevent Bigtable emulator and server invalid timestamp errors.
- Resolved row key collisions in layerwise serving by suffixing @layer_{layer_id} in BigtableConnector and L2 adapter.
- Bypassed 200MB mutation size limits with concurrent split mutations and added 90MB single-shard safety warnings.
- Fixed V2 in-process memory exhaustion reference leak inside LMCacheEngine.retrieve by releasing reference counts for hits.
- Formatted all files with isort and ruff format to comply with Google Python style guide and pre-commit checks.

- Offloaded memoryview-to-bytes conversion to executor thread pool.
- Fixed circuit breaker cache miss reset logic when no errors occur.
- Reconciled storage accounting (ghost bytes) on lookup and load cache misses.
- Rolled back lock refcounts on lookup cancellation or failure.
- Implemented size-based batch mutations chunking for unsharded bulk store.
- Added comprehensive unit tests for all correctness fixes.

[ROCm] Build and publish prebuilt gfx942/gfx950 wheel (#4273)

* [ROCm] Build and publish prebuilt gfx942/gfx950 wheel

Adds a release path for the ROCm/HIP wheel so AMD Instinct users can
`pip install` LMCache into an upstream vllm/vllm-openai-rocm container
instead of building from source (parity with the CUDA cu129 flow).

The wheel is built in rocm/dev-ubuntu-22.04:7.2.3-complete against the
public torch==2.11.0+rocm7.2, so its C++ ABI matches the torch shipped in
vllm/vllm-openai-rocm (torch 2.11, ROCm 7.2, cp312). auditwheel excludes

SONAMEs so libamdhip64.so.7 / libhsa-runtime64.so.1 are not vendored),
leaving a lean 7.5 MB wheel that binds to the host image at runtime --
same policy as the cu129 wheel excluding libcudart. PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH
bakes gfx942 (MI300X/MI325X) and gfx950 (MI350X/MI355X) into one fat
binary.

- .github/workflows/build_rocm_artifacts.yml: reusable build workflow

- .github/scripts/build_rocm_wheel.sh: container build + auditwheel repair.
- .github/scripts/smoke_test_rocm_wheel.sh: install into the vLLM ROCm
  image, load c_ops, and run the real KV-transfer kernels on-device.
- publish.yml: build-rocm job + publish-rocm-github-release (attaches the
  wheel to a v{tag}-rocm GitHub Release, not PyPI; mirrors cu129).
- docs: prebuilt-wheel install tab for the upstream vLLM ROCm image.

Validated on MI350X (gfx950): the dev-ubuntu wheel built against public
torch loads against the image's fork torch (2.11.0+gitd0c8b1f) and passes
all 56 tests/v1/test_mem_kernels.py cases on-device.

commits.message:
feat(valkey): Tag GLIDE connections as GlidePySync(lmcache:<ver>) (#4023)

* feat(valkey): Tag GLIDE connections as GlidePySync(lmcache:<ver>)

Attribute LMCache's valkey-glide connections in CLIENT INFO / CLIENT LIST
via GLIDE's client_info_tag option, producing GlidePySync(lmcache:<version>)
so LMCache usage is distinguishable without disturbing GLIDE's own library
identity or adoption metrics.

client_info_tag was added to the glide Python client in valkey-io/valkey-glide#6389
and ships in valkey-glide 2.5.0; it is not in any released wheel yet. Older
clients would raise TypeError on the unknown kwarg, so the connector applies
the tag only behind a feature-detection guard: it inspects the client config
constructor signature for a client_info_tag parameter and passes it through
in both the standalone and cluster branches of _ThreadWorkerPool._get_client
only when present. Behavior on current glide builds is unchanged.

The tag falls back to a bare "lmcache" if the resolved version string
contains whitespace (which GLIDE's config validation rejects).

Adds tests covering tag formatting, the whitespace fallback, signature-based
support detection, and that _get_client sets/omits the kwarg for supported
vs unsupported glide builds (standalone and cluster) using an injected fake
glide_sync module.

Signed-off-by: Omer Rubinstein <omerrubi@amazon.com>

* style(valkey): Fix isort import ordering in client_info_tag tests

isort (repo pre-commit hook, PyCQA/isort) orders the imported names
case-insensitively, placing _ThreadWorkerPool after the lowercase
helper functions. Reorder to satisfy the hook; local ruff check did not
flag it. No functional change.

Signed-off-by: Omer Rubinstein <omerrubi@amazon.com>

* test(valkey): Make client_info_tag test fake mypy-clean

CI mypy flagged the fake glide_sync helper: the config classes were
redefined under if/else (no-redef) and attributes were assigned onto a
types.ModuleType instance (attr-defined).

Rework the fake so it is statically clean:
- Define tagged vs untagged client/cluster config classes as distinct

- Build the fake module as a types.SimpleNamespace rather than assigning

- Annotate the empty kwargs dict (var-annotated).

Verified locally: mypy, isort, ruff check/format all clean; 10 tests pass.

commits.author: Arijit Desai
commits.message:
fix(pd): fail fast when a prefill exceeds the receiver buffer capacity (#4210)

The receiver's reservation admission only succeeds when the buffer has
enough free chunks (`available >= total_chunks`), and `available` can
never exceed the buffer's total capacity. A request whose declared
`total_chunks` is larger than the whole buffer therefore can never be
admitted: it blocked for the full `pd_allocation_timeout_sec` and then
raised a misleading "over-subscribed" timeout, tearing down the transfer
mid-flight (clients saw ServerDisconnectedError / "Not enough data to
satisfy transfer length header").

Add an explicit fail-fast in `_async_allocate_and_put`, co-located with
the existing `total_chunks == 0` validation, that rejects such a request
immediately with an actionable error (needs N chunks, buffer holds M,
increase pd_buffer_size). Add a regression test asserting the request is
rejected well before the admission timeout could elapse and leaves no
reservation behind.

Signed-off-by: ardecode <desaiarijit@gmail.com>

commits.author: Libin Tang
commits.message:
xpu: pin LMCache host buffer via sycl::malloc_host (#4129)

* xpu: pin LMCache host buffer via sycl::malloc_host

The local_cpu backend host buffer was never pinned on XPU: the pinned-alloc
path (lmc_ops.alloc_pinned_ptr) is CUDA-only (cudaHostAlloc) and is not
compiled into xpu_ops, so allocation silently fell back to pageable host
memory -> D2H KV store ran at ~1.5 GB/s.

Add a SYCL analog alloc_pinned_ptr/free_pinned_ptr (sycl::malloc_host on the
current XPU device context) bound under the same names as the CUDA ops, so
lmcache._get_backend() overrides them by name on XPU with no device-specific
branching in _allocate_cpu_memory/_free_cpu_memory. Restores true USM-pinned
host memory -> D2H store ~10-30 GB/s (~20x).

sycl::malloc_host is capped at the device max_mem_alloc_size (~30 GiB on B70
= 95% of one card's VRAM), so a large max_local_cpu_size can overflow it.
Add a device-agnostic pageable fallback (with a warning) so the engine
degrades gracefully instead of crashing; torch pin_memory=True is avoided
because torch XPU pinned buffers segfault on access above ~16 GiB. shm /
NUMA / hugepage allocations are excluded from the fallback since a plain
pageable buffer cannot preserve their semantics.

Split out of #4022 (pin-memory allocation only); the SGLang connector logic
changes in that PR are being tracked separately.
